layers.note: Multiply. Clipped to a max factor of 1.0 -- loses a small (~1.22x ceiling) highlight boost real Multiply blending cannot express; everything else is exact.
Multiply. RGB is the tint FACTOR relative to the paper colour, not the raw landuse colour -- looks unfamiliar at face value in Normal blend, correct once set to Multiply.

Multiply. Legal land-use zoning (用途地域) from MLIT A29, in the conventional Japanese zoning-map colours -- residential greens, commercial pinks, industrial blues. Separate from the buildings layer on purpose: it says what the ground is ZONED for, which is not the same as what is built on it.
Walls, seawalls, retaining walls, fences and hedges (OSM barrier=*). Weighted by kind -- a seawall draws heavier than a hedge.
Multiply. Exact -- this multiplier is mathematically bounded to [castShadowFloor, 1.0] and never needs to brighten, unlike hillshade.
Building cast shadows only (Minkowski sweep). Bridge shadows live in the 'bridges' layer instead, matching the original's own separate always-on-top bridge pass.
Bridge decks + their own shadow, redrawn on top of everything below -- never shadow-multiplied.
Transmission and distribution lines, their pylons/poles, and substations/plants. Drawn in red on purpose (direct request) so the grid reads as infrastructure, not terrain.
man_made=* -- the small vertical stuff (silos, tanks, chimneys, cranes, masts, water towers) as point marks, plus linear/area works (piers, breakwaters, quays, embankments) as outlines.
Shrines, monuments, ruins, forts and archaeological sites. Wayside shrines dominate the count in this frame.
Civic services, glyph-coded by kind: cross = medical, square = police/fire, triangle = education, circle = civic/worship.
Designated evacuation/assembly points, in signage green (matching real Japanese evacuation signing). Given its own layer and heavier marks deliberately.

Place-name labels (city/town/suburb/quarter/neighbourhood), sized by rank, Japanese over romanised. Placement is collision-avoided and computed over the WHOLE frame deterministically, so a label never half- appears at a tile seam.
New reference overlay, not part of the map's own look.
New reference overlay. Numbered col,row from the frame's own origin -- consistent across tiles.

howToUse: Stack files in ascending index order (00 at the bottom), each set to the listed blendMode. Layers not generated here (paper grain/vignette, road/place labels, cartouche, compass rose) are intentionally out of scope -- see tools/city-map/README.md.
